8.01.name: Physics I
8.01.summary: Introductory classical mechanics taught through technology-enabled active learning.
notes: Placement depends on the first-year Math Skills Assessment.
8.01.policy_summary: Physics I placement uses the Math Skills Assessment. The longer8.01L route continues through IAP, with concurrent Calculus I recommended. Spring8.011 is for students who did not pass fall8.01. The deeper8.012 route is intended for stronger preparation; students already holding8.01 credit receive six elective units for8.012 rather than a new twelve-unit GIR credit. Intended preparation and recommendations are not silently formal prerequisites.
8.01.rationale: The actual first-year advising section describes classical mechanics or electricity and magnetism; the subject is a physical-science application/domain, not computing foundations or AI methods.

8.01L.summary: The longer classical-mechanics route covers the same material and depth as8.01, extending through January IAP.
notes: Offered in fall with IAP completion in the advising description; intended for first-year students with little calculus-based physics. Concurrent Calculus I is recommended; this wording does not establish a formal co-requisite.
8.01L.rationale: The actual first-year advising section describes classical mechanics or electricity and magnetism; the subject is a physical-science application/domain, not computing foundations or AI methods.

8.011.name: Physics I
8.011.summary: Spring classical-mechanics version covering the same material as8.01 for students who did not pass the fall course.
8.011.prerequisites: For students who do not pass 8.01 in the fall.
notes: Conditional repeat route; not a new fixed subject for every student.
8.011.rationale: The actual first-year advising section describes classical mechanics or electricity and magnetism; the subject is a physical-science application/domain, not computing foundations or AI methods.

8.012.summary: A deeper classical-mechanics route for students with strong physics and mathematics preparation, including more demanding problem sets.
notes: Students already holding8.01 credit who take8.012 receive six elective units. This conditional repeat-credit rule does not replace the regular GIR course-credit observation. AP/ASE preparation is described as intended background, not a universal admission prerequisite.
8.012.rationale: The actual first-year advising section describes classical mechanics or electricity and magnetism; the subject is a physical-science application/domain, not computing foundations or AI methods.

8.02.name: Physics II
8.02.summary: Introductory electricity and magnetism using technology-enabled active learning.
8.02.policy_summary: The first-year advising page requires credit in Physics I8.01 and Calculus I18.01 before enrolling in8.02. It presents8.022 as a more mathematically advanced Physics II alternative for stronger preparation; the page does not supply that variant's full formal prerequisite statement.
8.02.rationale: The actual first-year advising section describes classical mechanics or electricity and magnetism; the subject is a physical-science application/domain, not computing foundations or AI methods.

8.022.summary: The more mathematically advanced electricity-and-magnetism route, intended for students with a strong physics and mathematics background.
notes: Fall and spring offerings are stated in the advising page; formal prerequisite details are not supplied there.
8.022.rationale: The actual first-year advising section describes classical mechanics or electricity and magnetism; the subject is a physical-science application/domain, not computing foundations or AI methods.

18.01L.name: Calculus
18.01L.summary: Calculus course with an emphasis on accessible mathematical learning; the public page gives meeting information and grading weights.
notes: Public Canvas syllabus page verified for Fall Term AY2026–2027. The page links a separate Course Syllabus document, which has not been read; detailed topics, prerequisites and credit amounts are not inferred from the welcome text. The public course page is accessible without login.
18.01L.rationale: The actual public course page explicitly identifies calculus; this is a bounded subject identification, not a full topic-by-topic syllabus review.
